Subject: DPA & SCC module clarification — post-demo recap and next steps

Hi Matthew — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your legal/procurement teams have something to action: 

Call highlights:
- Fintecta's main asks: confirmation on Redwood's role (controller vs. processor), preferred SCC module for cross-border transfers, and SOC 2 evidence (Type II).
- You confirmed initial volume profile and that a DPA + SCC will be required for procurement.

Redwood posture (high level):
- Default: Redwood operates as a Processor when customers send customer data to our hosted APIs. We act on customer instructions and can sign a standard DPA reflecting that relationship.
- Controller exceptions: For customers requiring Redwood to make independent determinations about purposes/means (rare), we can discuss language, but that typically requires a different contractual approach and product configuration.
- SCC modules: For processor scenarios we typically propose the processor-focused SCC module (Module 2 / Processor-to-processor language). If you need Redwood to accept controller obligations we can evaluate Module 1 scenarios, but that'll be an exception.
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II controls; latest audit completed in Q2 2026. We can share a redacted SOC 2 report under NDA or via a secure evidence portal.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I attached a draft Redwood DPA for your review (Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf). Please flag any redlines or specific obligations you need us to accept.
2) If helpful, we can kick off a short legal-to-legal working call (30 mins) next week to walk the DPA and SCC module choices.
3) Ben (cc) will start the vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) intake for Fintecta so you can see the scope of controls we capture. You should receive an email with a VSQ link.

Would you like us to send the DPA via DocuSign once you confirm markup preferences? Also, let me know your procurement timeline so we can prioritize the SOC 2 evidence flow.

Thanks —
Olga

Matthew — thanks for the quick follow-up. Short answers below, followed by proposed concrete items for your legal team: 

1) SCC module: For the common hosted-API Processor scenario we propose the EU Commission's standard Contractual Clauses for controller-to-processor transfers, implemented via the Processor module (commonly referred to as the Module 2/Processor addendum in our DPA package). I will flag the exact clause references in the DPA cover page so privacy counsel can review quickly.

2) SOC 2: Redwood's last Type II audit in Q2 2026 had no high-severity exceptions; there were two operational observations that are remediated and documented in the audit response. We can provide a redacted report and a short summary (bridge letter) under NDA.

3) Hybrid use-case: If Fintecta requires Redwood to independently determine purposes/means (e.g., performing enrichment that changes processing purpose), that would push toward a controller-or-joint-controller discussion. Practically: we can accept some additional responsibilities but it typically requires targeted contract language and product configuration (e.g., restricting autonomous enrichment unless an explicit controller instruction is present). I suggest legal-to-legal to map the exact use cases.

Proposed next steps for efficiency: 
- I have attached the DPA draft (same as earlier). Please have counsel mark the DPA with preferred SCC module and any clauses that would push Redwood into controller-like obligations.
- Ben will send the VSQ to procurement@fintecta.io shortly (link below). Completing that will speed SOC 2 evidence and architecture questions.
- If you confirm a legal call, Ben + Laura will join from Redwood. Suggested windows: Thu 22 Oct 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 23 Oct 09:00–10:00 PT.

Subject: Technical notes for Fintecta — data flows and retention options

Laura / Olga — dropping the technical call notes that might be helpful for Matthews' engineering and privacy teams: 

- Data flow: Fintecta -> Redwood Hosted API (EU region available) -> optional KV caching for prompt reuse. Default is ephemeral KV cache (TTL 1 hour) unless customer requests longer retention.
- Retention/Deletion: We support customer-controlled retention windows; for regulated customers we offer Private deployment or VPC connectors with no telemetry retention.
- Access controls: Role-based access + audit logging; access to production logs limited to on-call SRE and anonymized for support cases.
- Encryption: Data encrypted in transit (TLS1.3) and at rest (AES-256). Keys managed via our KMS; customer-managed keys available on Redwood Private.
- SOC 2 evidence: mapping doc and control narratives are available for common queries.

If Fintecta flags a particular enrichment workflow that might create a purpose-determining action, we should capture that in a short appendix to the DPA describing the permitted enrichment scope (and disallowed autonomous decisions).

Ben
